## Real Property Tax Circuit Breaker and Form IT-214

Form IT-214 is for the Real Property Tax Credit, New York's refundable "circuit breaker" credit for qualifying homeowners and renters that provides targeted relief when property taxes or rent consume too high a portion of a household's income.

### Federal Adjusted Gross Income (FAGI) Requirements

Form IT‐214 provides a refundable Real Property Tax Credit for homeowners and renters with federal adjusted gross income (FAGI) of $18,000 or less. However, the limit increases to $58,400 if you or your spouse was age 65 or older by the end of the year.

### 2024 Changes

New York State no longer uses Form IT‑229 (Real Property Tax Relief Credit) for tax year 2024 and forward, as the IT‑229 form has been discontinued for tax year 2024. New York's remaining refundable property-related credit is the Real Property Tax Credit, claimed on Form IT‑214.

### How the Credit Works

The credit functions as a true "circuit breaker" and reimburses you for a portion of the property tax (or rent-equivalent) burden that exceeds a specific percentage of your income.

## Real Property Tax Circuit Breaker and Form IT-214

Form IT-214 is for the Real Property Tax Credit, New York's refundable "circuit breaker" credit for qualifying homeowners and renters that provides targeted relief when property taxes or rent consume too high a portion of a household's income.

### Federal Adjusted Gross Income (FAGI) Requirements

Form IT‐214 provides a refundable Real Property Tax Credit for homeowners and renters with federal adjusted gross income (FAGI) of $18,000 or less. However, the limit increases to $58,400 if you or your spouse was age 65 or older by the end of the year.

### 2024 Changes

New York State no longer uses Form IT‑229 (Real Property Tax Relief Credit) for tax year 2024 and forward, as the IT‑229 form has been discontinued for tax year 2024. New York's remaining refundable property-related credit is the Real Property Tax Credit, claimed on Form IT‑214.

### How the Credit Works

The credit functions as a true "circuit breaker" and reimburses you for a portion of the property tax (or rent-equivalent) burden that exceeds a specific percentage of your income.

"You are entitled to this refundable credit if: your federal adjusted gross income is $18,000 or less; you occupied the same New York residence for six months or more; you were a New York State resident for the entire tax year; you could not be claimed as a dependent on another taxpayer's federal income tax return; your residence was not completely exempted from real property taxes; the current market value of all real property you owned, such as houses, garages, and land, was $85,000 or less; and you meet all the conditions listed under either Homeowners or Renters below."

# Social Security Benefits Taxation Under § 86

## Provisional Income Calculation

Per §86(a)(1) and (b)(1), a taxpayer's gross income includes Social Security benefits when their "modified adjusted gross income" plus "one-half of the social security benefits" exceeds a threshold.

## Base Amount Threshold

Under §86(c)(1), the foundational threshold is "$25,000" for single filers, though this increases to $32,000 for joint returns.

## How It Works

The taxation mechanism operates in two tiers: up to 50% of benefits become taxable if income crosses the initial threshold, with an additional 85% potentially taxable at higher income levels under §86(a)(2).
